title: Unvalidated limit can disable pagination on /runs

evidence.quote:
async def list_media_runs(
    limit: int = 20,
    session: Session = Depends(get_session),
):
    """List recent media processing pipeline runs."""
    runs = session.exec(
        select(MediaProcessingRun)
        .order_by(MediaProcessingRun.started_at.desc())
        .limit(limit)

reasoning: The route exposes limit directly as a query parameter and passes it to SQLAlchemy without a lower or upper bound. In SQLite, negative LIMIT values such as -1 mean no limit, so an authenticated request to GET /runs?limit=-1 can return the entire processing history. Very large positive values can also produce unexpectedly large queries and responses. This defeats the route's 'recent runs' behavior and creates a resource-exhaustion risk as the run table grows.
reproduction: Call GET /runs?limit=-1 against a database with many media_processing_runs rows; SQLite will return all rows instead of rejecting the request or keeping the default page size.
recommendation: Validate the query parameter with FastAPI Query constraints, for example limit: int = Query(default=20, ge=1, le=100), and choose a project-appropriate maximum.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the route currently has no validation contract asserted around negative or very large limit values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API test that GET /runs?limit=-1 returns 422, GET /runs?limit=1000 returns 422 if the maximum is lower, and the default request returns at most the default number of runs ordered by started_at descending.
minimumFixScope: Update only list_media_runs to constrain the limit query parameter and add focused route tests for limit validation and ordering.
